chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: Inform me about the best of the times for salat al-fajr.
He said: At the rising of the fajr.
Indeed Allah says: “Indeed, the Qur'an of fajr is ever witnessed.”

Meaning salat al-fajr: the angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it. So when the servant performs salat al-subh at the rising of the fajr, it is recorded for him twice: the angels of the night record it and the angels of the day record it.

key_terms.قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ: the recitation or prayer of dawn, interpreted here as salat al-fajr
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةُ اللَّيْلِ: the angels assigned to the night
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةُ النَّهَارِ: the angels assigned to the day

ai.seo_question: What is the best time to perform salat al-fajr according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the most excellent time for salat al-fajr is at the rising of fajr. It explains the Qur'anic phrase “إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا” as referring to salat al-fajr, which is witnessed by both the angels of the night and the angels of the day. Because of this, one who performs it at that time has it recorded twice.
